title: Quarter Volume Library Prep Step 5: Size Selection
author: Opentrons
materials: The protocol will alert the user to ensure reagents are present on deck in sufficient volume.

steps.title: Set magnetic engage height
steps.instruction: Enter the magnetic module engage height for the custom labware as a protocol parameter before starting.

steps.title: Verify reagent volumes
steps.instruction: Confirm that all required reagents are loaded on the deck in sufficient volume as the protocol will alert you.

steps.title: Deliver water (if needed)
steps.instruction: Using the P300 multi‑channel pipette, dispense water into the wells of the magnetic module plate as required based on fragment size.

steps.title: Add first beads and mix
steps.instruction: Using either the P20 or P300 multi‑channel pipette, add the first bead suspension to each well of the magnetic module plate (volume depends on fragment size) and mix the contents.

steps.title: Incubate and transfer supernatant
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate for 5 minutes, engage the magnets, then use the P300 multi‑channel pipette to transfer the first bead supernatant to the size selection plate.

steps.title: Move size plate to magnet
steps.instruction: When prompted, pause the OT‑2 and manually relocate the size plate from slot 3 to the magnetic module.

steps.title: Add second beads and mix
steps.instruction: Using the P20 multi‑channel pipette, dispense the second bead suspension into each well of the magnetic module plate and mix.

steps.title: Incubate and discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Incubate for 5 minutes, engage the magnets, then use the P300 multi‑channel pipette to discard the second bead supernatant into liquid waste.

steps.title: Wash bead pellets
steps.instruction: Wash the bead pellets twice with 80 % ethanol using the P300 multi‑channel pipette.

steps.title: Resuspend beads, incubate, engage
steps.instruction: After air drying, resuspend the bead pellets in 1× TE with the P20 multi‑channel pipette, incubate for 2 minutes, then engage the magnets.
